title: Multiplying monomials

worked_examples.misconception: Adding 3 and 2 instead of finding three groups of 2x.
worked_examples.repair: Draw three rows of two x tiles and count six.

steps.title: Build groups
steps.action: Place two x tiles in each of three rows.
steps.narration: Three groups each hold two copies of x.

steps.title: Count coefficients
steps.action: Count the six x tiles without changing their unit.
steps.narration: Three multiplied by two gives six copies of x.

steps.title: Write one term
steps.action: Write the total coefficient beside the x unit.
steps.narration: The product is six x, with x to the first power.

worked_examples.repair: Represent two negative rows of three a tiles.

steps.title: Read the signs
steps.action: Highlight the negative first factor and positive second factor.
steps.narration: One negative factor makes the product negative.

steps.title: Multiply magnitudes
steps.action: Count two groups of three a.
steps.narration: Two times three is six copies of a.

steps.title: Attach the sign
steps.action: Write the minus in front of 6a.
steps.narration: The signed answer is negative six a.

worked_examples.misconception: Turning x into x² although the other factor contains no x.
worked_examples.repair: Count three lots of four x; keep one variable factor.

steps.title: Repeat the x group
steps.action: Show three groups of four x tiles.
steps.narration: The plain number repeats the existing x group three times.

steps.title: Multiply numbers
steps.action: Multiply four by three.
steps.narration: Twelve x tiles appear in all.

steps.title: Retain the variable
steps.action: Write twelve times x, with no new x factor.
steps.narration: The answer has x to the first power.

worked_examples.misconception: Writing 6x because the second x factor was ignored.
worked_examples.repair: Construct a 2x by 3x rectangle; count square x-by-x tiles.

steps.title: Multiply each kind
steps.action: Pair the coefficients and pair the variable factors.
steps.narration: Two times three determines the number of x-by-x tiles.

steps.title: Name the area unit
steps.action: Show x times x as one x² square.
steps.narration: Two copies of x multiply to x squared, rather than x.

steps.title: Write area term
steps.action: Combine six squares into one algebraic term.
steps.narration: Six x-squared units give six x squared.

worked_examples.misconception: Combining a and b as though they were like terms.
worked_examples.repair: Use a-length and b-width; each unit square has area ab.

steps.title: Separate factors
steps.action: Select 4 and 2, then a and b.
steps.narration: Numbers multiply together; the different variable factors both remain.

steps.title: Count area tiles
steps.action: Show eight rectangles, each with sides a and b.
steps.narration: Each rectangle has area ab, and there are eight.

steps.title: Write product
steps.action: Combine the count and unit ab.
steps.narration: The product is eight ab, not eight a plus b.

worked_examples.skill: Two negatives give a positive product
worked_examples.misconception: Keeping a negative sign or omitting one m factor.
worked_examples.repair: Pair sign badges first, then join two m lengths into square tiles.

steps.title: Resolve signs
steps.action: Highlight both negative factors.
steps.narration: A negative times a negative produces a positive product.

steps.title: Multiply variable factors
steps.action: Form m-by-m squares from the two m factors.
steps.narration: Each m times m becomes m squared.

steps.title: Finish coefficients
steps.action: Multiply three by two and retain the positive sign.
steps.narration: Six positive m-squared units remain.

worked_examples.misconception: Adding coefficients but also adding variables as x²+x.
worked_examples.repair: Show two x factors from x² and one more from x.

steps.title: Expand variable factors
steps.action: Show x² as x times x, then one more x.
steps.narration: The exponent tells us there are already two x factors.

steps.title: Count factors
steps.action: Stack all three x factors together.
steps.narration: Multiplication combines two x factors and one x factor into x cubed.

steps.title: Multiply coefficients
steps.action: Multiply three by two and keep the three x factors.
steps.narration: The coefficient is six and the power is three.

worked_examples.misconception: Reporting -5q² after ignoring the zero factor.
worked_examples.repair: Show an empty set of rows; no product tiles can appear.

steps.title: Show zero groups
steps.action: Remove every repeated row.
steps.narration: Zero groups means there are no tiles to count.

steps.title: Apply the zero rule
steps.action: Observe that any second factor still gives no groups.
steps.narration: Multiplication by zero has value zero for every q.

steps.title: Write numeric result
steps.action: Write zero without a variable part.
steps.narration: The product is zero, rather than a signed q term.

worked_examples.verify: At q=3, 0×(-45)=0 and the answer is 0.

worked_examples.misconception: Multiplying by two instead of by one half, or leaving x to the first power.
worked_examples.repair: Partition six x-length columns into two halves; each tile has x×x area.

steps.title: Split the coefficient
steps.action: Take half of six, keeping the variable factors aside.
steps.narration: One half of six is three.

steps.title: Pair variable factors
steps.action: Join one x from each factor into an x² square.
steps.narration: The x factors multiply into x squared.

steps.title: Write product
steps.action: Combine three with x squared.
steps.narration: There are three x-squared tiles.

worked_examples.misconception: Dropping a negative factor or changing b into a.
worked_examples.repair: Pair both negative signs; stack two a factors and retain b.

steps.title: Resolve three signs
steps.action: Pair the negative signs in first and third factors.
steps.narration: Two negatives cancel to make this product positive.

steps.title: Sort variable factors
steps.action: Place both a factors together and b apart.
steps.narration: a times a is a squared; b is a separate factor.

steps.title: Multiply numbers
steps.action: Multiply two, three and one, then attach a²b.
steps.narration: The complete product is positive six a squared b.

worked_examples.q: A tile has sides 3t cm and 4t cm. Find its area in cm² and evaluate at t=2.
worked_examples.misconception: Adding sides as a perimeter or reporting a linear unit.
worked_examples.repair: Grow a 3-by-4 area grid whose little square side is t cm.

steps.title: Construct area grid
steps.action: Mark three rows and four columns of t-by-t squares.
steps.narration: Area counts square units: each small square is t centimetres by t centimetres.

steps.title: Multiply symbolic sides
steps.action: Count twelve squares and label each t squared.
steps.narration: Three times four gives twelve, while t times t gives t squared.

steps.title: Evaluate given value
steps.action: Substitute two into the completed area formula.
steps.narration: Twelve times four is forty-eight square centimetres.

worked_examples.verify: Direct sides at t=2 are 6 cm and 8 cm; 6×8=48 cm².

worked_examples.q: A learner wrote (2x²)(3x)=6x². Identify the missing operation and correct the result.
worked_examples.answer: They omitted the second factor of x; the product is 6x³.
worked_examples.misconception: Treating an exponent as a decoration rather than a count of factors.
worked_examples.repair: Expose three x chips: x×x from x² and one x from the second term.

steps.title: Find omitted factor
steps.action: Compare the learner line with the three x chips in the original.
steps.narration: The second factor contributes a third x that cannot disappear.

steps.title: Recount powers
steps.action: Count two x factors plus one x factor.
steps.narration: There are three x factors, so the exponent is three.

steps.title: Repair the line
steps.action: Keep six as coefficient and replace x² with x³.
steps.narration: The repaired answer is six x cubed.

worked_examples.verify: At x=2, original 8×6=48, wrong 6x²=24, and corrected 6x³=48.

worked_examples.skill: Cost per learner in grouped packs
worked_examples.q: A school buys 4 packs of 3n notebooks at R2 each. Express the total cost in rand and check n=5.
worked_examples.misconception: Multiplying only four by three and forgetting the price factor.
worked_examples.repair: Show four pack trays, three n notebooks per tray, and a R2 badge on each notebook.

steps.title: Count notebooks
steps.action: Show four groups of three n notebooks.
steps.narration: Four groups of three n make twelve n notebooks.

steps.title: Apply unit price
steps.action: Attach the two-rand badge to each notebook.
steps.narration: Each of the twelve n notebooks costs two rand.

steps.title: Substitute n
steps.action: Multiply twenty-four by five.
steps.narration: The total is one hundred and twenty rand when n is five.

worked_examples.q: Simplify (-2p)² and explain why the result is positive.
worked_examples.misconception: Squaring only p or keeping a negative result after multiplying two negatives.
worked_examples.repair: Show two complete copies of the bracket, with two negative badges.

steps.title: Expand the square
steps.action: Replace the exponent 2 with two complete (-2p) factors.
steps.narration: The square applies to the signed coefficient and to p.

steps.title: Resolve signs and powers
steps.action: Pair negative badges and join the two p factors.
steps.narration: Two negatives give a positive; p times p gives p squared.

steps.title: Multiply magnitudes
steps.action: Multiply two by two after resolving the signs.
steps.narration: The result is positive four p squared.

worked_examples.skill: Compare area expressions across two tiles
worked_examples.q: One square has side 2x cm. A rectangle has sides x cm and 3x cm. Find both areas, then the difference square minus rectangle.
worked_examples.answer: Square: 4x² cm²; rectangle: 3x² cm²; difference x² cm².
worked_examples.misconception: Adding side lengths or treating x² and x as interchangeable.
worked_examples.repair: Build two scaled area grids: four x² squares beside three x² squares.

steps.title: Build both grids
steps.action: Draw a 2-by-2 square grid and a 1-by-3 rectangle grid.
steps.narration: The first area has four x-squared tiles; the second has three.

steps.title: Compare like area units
steps.action: Align the x-squared tiles and subtract three from four.
steps.narration: Both are areas, so subtract only their counts of identical x-squared tiles.

steps.title: Write the difference
steps.action: Show one unmatched x² tile with square-centimetre units.
steps.narration: The square exceeds the rectangle by x squared square centimetres.

worked_examples.verify: At x=2, square 16 cm², rectangle 12 cm²; difference 4 cm² equals x² cm².

practice_questions: 6×2=12, so there is still one x factor.
Two m factors form an m-by-m square.
Zero times any expression equals zero.
One third of nine is three.
A rectangle has sides 2k cm and 7k cm. Find its area.
Multiply lengths and use square units.
2×7=14 and k×k=k², so area is 14k² cm².
A learner says 4x² × 2x = 8x². Give the correct product.
Count x×x and the additional x.
Three crates each hold 4n pencils at R2 per pencil. Write the total cost.
Multiply crates, pencils and rand per pencil.
A square has side 3z cm and a rectangle sides z cm and 5z cm. How much larger is the square area?
mastery_questions: Seven groups of 2n give fourteen n.
The two signs give positive; 2×5=10 and x×x=x².
A learner writes (-3p)²=-9p². Identify the first wrong action and correct it.
The square applies to the whole signed term; the result is 9p².
(-3p)(-3p)=9p²; two negatives give a positive product.
A rectangle has sides 2x cm and 3x cm; a square has side x cm. Find their area difference and verify at x=2.
5x² cm²; at x=2 the difference is 20 cm².
Rectangle area 6x²; square x²; difference 5x²; at x=2, 24-4=20.
reassessment_questions: Two negatives make a positive and t×t=t².
Multiply coefficients; count three y factors.
A square has side 3p cm; a rectangle has sides 2p cm and 4p cm. Find area difference and verify p=2.
p² cm²; at p=2 the difference is 4 cm².
